result:
I'd make people more curious.

Not just casually interested in things, but genuinely driven to understand how the world actually works — physics, biology, economics, human nature, history, and all the messy interactions between them. A deep, almost instinctive discomfort with "I don't know" or "that's just how it is."

Most of the world's biggest problems aren't caused by a lack of resources or technology. They're caused by people being bad at seeing reality clearly and updating their beliefs when evidence contradicts them. If curiosity became a dominant human trait instead of tribal loyalty, status-seeking, or short-term comfort, a lot of downstream problems would sort themselves out over time: bad policies, ideological capture, scientific stagnation, and even a lot of conflict.

Everything else — better governance, reduced suffering, technological progress — tends to follow from people actually wanting to know what's true rather than wanting to be right.
